abstract: Online political discussions increasingly involve AI-mediated participation, as users invoke LLMs to assess contested claims, arbitrate disputes, and respond to opposing viewpoints. As these systems become participants in online exchanges, they may alter which speakers and argumentative strategies receive validation within the discussion.   We study this interactional dimension by reconstructing 5,376 Debate.org debates as LLM conversations and running nearly 150,000 controlled multi-turn conversations that vary user political orientation, expertise, rhetorical strategy, and defended position, including conversations with competing users.   Across naturalistic and controlled debates, we find that LLMs are systematically more receptive to left-leaning than right-leaning users. The asymmetry persists when users with different political orientations defend the same position and when opposing users appear in the same conversation, indicating that it is not fully explained by stance agreement or simple accommodation to the current speaker. Repeated interaction increases receptiveness without eliminating this ordering; expertise also matters, while rhetorical differences are smaller. The pattern appears across multiple models, but is not fixed: fine-tuning on different political corpora can largely erase or reverse it. These results show that LLMs can respond systematically differently to participants in the same political debate, making such interactional asymmetries important for understanding their emerging role in online public discourse.

ur.ai_reason: 受控实验分析用户属性对LLM辩论回应的影响
ur.tldr: 将5,376场Debate.org辩论重构为LLM对话并开展近15万次受控多轮实验，发现模型对左倾用户的接纳度系统性高于右倾用户，且不能由立场一致完全解释。专业度会影响结果，论证策略差异较小；微调政治语料可消除甚至逆转偏差，表明偏差具有训练依赖性。

title: User Attributes and Political Ideology Shape LLM Receptiveness in Online Political Debates
title_zh: 用户属性与政治意识形态塑造LLM在在线政治辩论中的接受倾向
